title: Kiwi air customer complaint
titleCn: Kiwi Air客服投诉：网上订票儿童票价出错

paragraphs.text: Kiwi Air. Good morning. You're speaking with Roger. How may I help you?
Yes. Hi. My name's Janet. I've just been trying to make a booking on the Internet, and I'm having a problem that I'd like to complain about.
So let me just take down your full name.
It's Janet Quigley. That's Q-U-I-G-L-E-Y.
Thank you. And what's the problem exactly?

Well, yes. I'm trying to book myself and three children, so four tickets to fly within New Zealand. We're wanting to fly from Wellington to Christchurch. Not one way, I mean, but return. So it's just a simple booking.
Yes. And you've put your dates in, have you?
Yes. The dates are... Um, what are we in now? It's September, isn't it? So I'm booking for October. Oh, sorry. I mean November, the tenth till the fifteenth.
Right. Let me just get that down on the form. And what time would that be?
We'd be leaving at 11:45 in the morning, arriving into Christchurch at 12:30.
Mm-hmm.
I know that it's cheaper to not make the reservation in person, so to save paying the fee, I've been trying to do it through your homepage.
Yes. So what's the problem exactly?

Well, every time I put in a number of adults and children traveling, the website automatically alters the rate for one of the children to what you'd pay for an adult. It's very annoying. I'm getting so frustrated with it. And each time I change it back, I've been getting error messages telling me to call you directly. I really can't understand it.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to ten.
Now listen and answer questions five to ten.

All right. Well, yes, there is a reason for why that's happening. It's Kiwi Air policy, I'm afraid, to allow a maximum of two children to travel on child fares with just the one adult accompanying them.
So because there's three of them and just me, do you mean I have to pay an adult fare for one of my children?
Yes, that's right.
But I've flown to Australia before on my own with the children, and we didn't have to pay extra.
It's a policy that we've just introduced for domestic air travel. It may be extended later for international travel as well.

But an adult fare is for someone over the age of 12. My children are only 11, 8, and 5. It's not fair to charge them for an adult rate. Besides, they actually eat less than an adult, so they wouldn't consume as much food on the plane. I just don't think it's right.
Well, I'm sorry, but that's how we charge. We do look after children well on our flights, you know. We give them little packs of games and colored pencils so they have something to do, you know.

Well, still, the difference to pay between the fares is a lot of extra money that I hadn't budgeted for. It seems to me that your rules discriminate against a parent traveling on their own with the children and also families with lots of children. And what about school groups? That wouldn't be fair.
Well, madam, yes, I can see your point. You're welcome to put your complaint in writing if that's what you'd like to do.
Well, I certainly would. I'll be writing a letter to your customer services officer, is it?
Uh, just address it to the manager, then it will reach the right person. That's fine. That, that's your right to do that.
And how soon do you think they'll get back to me? I must say I really am shocked at this. I'm not happy about it at all.

Um, well, at busy times it sometimes takes a month, but it's low season now, so you should expect to receive a response probably inside a week. You need to take down this reference number. I'll just give it to you. It's GBK8422.
All right then. I'll put that in the letter.
Well, thanks for your help.
Thank you for calling Kiwi Air.
